content.thinking:
I'm figuring out the bone typing on the chain point, deciding to fall back to undefined when null, and opting to use chain.at(t) directly rather than the along method.

Now I'm working through concrete body geometry: defining the spine as a Catmull-Rom chain of five joints parented to the hips root, checking that the joint count matches the spans from the control points. I'm sketching a radius profile along the spine using interpolated keyframe values to shape the body's cross-section from rump to chest.

Adjusting the wheelbase to hind z -1.4, front z 0.85 for a more realistic stance, and shifting the rump cap start to -1.85 so it chains correctly to -2.3. I'm tuning the rx/ry radii arrays along the spine to shape the body profile smoothly from shoulder to rump.

Now I'm sketching the neck as a short chain of points rising from the chest toward the head, tapering the radius from 0.62 down to 0.55, with joint names for the base, middle, and tip so it can parent correctly onto the last spine joint.

Then I'm placing the head joint above the neck, aimed slightly downward, followed by a jaw pivot just behind the tusk base aimed further down for the bite motion. For the head geometry itself, I'm defining a cranium ellipsoid and checking its size against the neck and a potential crown bump, deciding to drop the crown since it's hidden inside the cranium, and instead planning a forehead shape before moving on to the face placement.

Still refining skull shapes... adding cheeks, a brow shelf via sticks, a trunk-base boss where the trunk emerges, and lip/tusk socket ellipsoids. I'm placing the trunk root, defining the lower jaw with a lighter chin tone and a darker pink lower lip ellipsoid, and setting up a dark mouth interior color.

I'm checking jaw visibility beneath the trunk base, making sure the chin reads correctly below the cheek from a side view. Then I'm positioning the tusks with curving root-to-tip points, but noticing the tusk x-position and radius may overlap slightly with the trunk's edge at certain heights, so I need to adjust spacing.

Pushing the tusk x-offsets outward to clear the trunk, and confirming total tusk length and tip placement extends beyond the trunk's silhouette. I'm setting up the tusk's tapered radius profile along a curved sweep path tied to the head bone, and now considering adding a short thickened ring at the base to represent the lip socket.

Now I'm working out the ear geometry: positioning the ear joint relative to the head, defining its outward-and-back orientation vector, and computing the plane normal from the cross product of the outline's local axes so the ear hangs naturally down and outward, mirroring the setup for the opposite side with flipped sign.

That span of ±1.4 feels too wide for real African elephant ears, which are more like 1.2m — so I should scale the outline down a bit, maybe width ~0.95 and height ~1.25, adjusting where the root sits near y=3.0-3.3.

Working out the ear shape with tapered thickness and a curved outward-facing outline, keeping the attach edge vertical so it fits cleanly against the head.

I'm positioning the ear joint slightly inward on the head and figuring out the right role (hinge vs fan) for its rotation behavior, while deciding to skip the rim-thickening detail for simplicity.

Now I'm grouping the ears together and moving on to eye placement — estimating cranium surface coordinates near z≈2.05 using the ellipsoid equation to position the eyes correctly below and ahead of the ears.

I realize the eye decal targets the cranium surface, but checking the cheek sphere's reach at that height shows it extends further out than the cranium does, meaning the cheek geometry likely covers the eye area instead.

Adding brow ridges...

Scaling the brow and eyelid geometry along the correct local axes so they elongate forward/back while staying thin against the surface normal, then setting up lash placement using a ring pattern around the eye with angle offsets tuned to orient lashes relative to world-up.

Actually I realize the lash ring's radius won't match the decal eye's elliptical shape, so I'll drop the separate lash geometry and let the eye texture carry the lash detail instead. Skipping the temporal gland streak too, and moving on to defining the trunk as a chain of points running from the head down to the tip, checking that the coordinates form a smooth curve.

I'm setting up the trunk's parent-child joint hierarchy, radius interpolation across its length, and section shape, then writing the paint logic for ridge-like texture rings along the trunk's surface using a sine-based pattern.

Adding torus rings for bark texture...

I'm skipping trunk wrinkles for simplicity, but want to shape the tip nicely — adding a small ellipsoid lip at the trunk's end with a forward-pointing spike, adjusting the tip's curl direction based on the path's tangent at the final point.

Adding tip cap and nostril details...

Now I'm checking the trunk tip's height above the ground, confirming it hangs with reasonable clearance, then moving on to planning the tail chain starting from the rump position.

I'll name the tail joints tail1-4 plus tailTip, tapering the radius along the sweep, and add a tuft of hair spikes ringed around the tip, tilted to hang downward along the tail's curve.

For the legs, I'm setting the hip joint position and adding a hamstring-shaped ellipsoid sized to blend with the rump width, matching it to the hip bone.

Working out the shoulder sphere dimensions and placement, then moving to the foot structure: a tapered cylinder for the foot body, a flat dark sole disc beneath it, and nail details to add next.

Placing nail positions with slightly tapered box geometry, sized so they sit just above the toe surface; going with 3 nails on hind feet and 4 on front feet using slightly different angular spreads to mimic real paw proportions.

Next I'm adding an ankle wrinkle ring using a torus, then handling foot surface coloring with dust tint based on height, and scattering crease-like cards across the body, neck, and leg surfaces with controlled spacing, lean angle, and flow direction so they look like natural skin folds.

For color I'm matching the cards to a muted gray-brown stroke tone so they blend subtly with the skin, then adding sparse dark bristle cards concentrated near the crown with a bit along the spine for texture variation.

I'm also adding mud splashes on the lower legs and belly using brown-toned textured cards, plus lightening the lower belly with paint and considering a small dark temporal gland stain, though I'm leaving dorsal ridge bristles out for now.

Checking the tusks and mouth area, I'm keeping the tusk tips slightly chipped with flat caps and leaving the lower lip and ear fold details simple. I'm also comparing the torso sweep against the leg placement, noting the front leg's outer edge extends slightly beyond the shoulder torso radius to form the shoulder muscle bulge.

Now I'm thinking through leg skinning and bone parenting -- legs attach to the spine joint but the sweep mesh stays separate from the body blend. I'm also planning to lighten the belly skin tone where the surface normal points downward, giving the underside a slightly pinker gray than the rest of the hide.

Setting up the skin color palette with mid, light, and dark grays plus dust tones, then writing the paint function that blends noise-driven color variation, cellular wrinkle darkening, and sinusoidal fold shading across the skin.

Still writing paint shader...

Checking the tuple return type infers correctly through contextual typing, then considering the cost: each texel requires 27 hash evaluations, which affects paint performance.

Now I'm defining the ear skin paint function, blending the base skin color with a pinkish tone using a radial falloff plus noise for texture, then adding angular vein patterns across the ear surface.

Writing tusk paint shader...

I also need to fix an unused parameter warning by renaming it, then move to the trunk paint shader, adding ridge striping based on position and a pinker tint toward the tip's underside using angular position in degrees.

Still writing eye SVG...

Still writing lash and crease paths...

Deciding to skip a separate ear rim and reuse the trunk skin paint for the ridge tori instead of a distinct darker tone, since flat shading with lighting should make the ridges read fine without needing a separate color.

Moving on to the body's bony features, I'm skipping extra details like scapula ridges or a tail root, and focusing instead on placing eyes and brows by raycasting against the head surface to find hit points for decal placement.

Still writing eye and brow placement...

I'll approximate the brow shape with a roughly circular scale since axis orientation isn't fully known, and place the lower eyelid pouch similarly using a downward offset from the hit point. For the skeleton, I'm tallying bone counts across hips, spine, neck, head, jaw, ears, trunk, tail, and legs to land around 40 total, keeping the rest pose neutral with trunk hanging straight and ears spread.

I'm naming the joint chains now, setting up spine joints parented to hips, then defining roles like "neck," "tail," "leg," and "tentacle," with consistent side-suffixed names for front and hind leg joints (shoulder, elbow, wrist, foot for front; hip, knee for hind).

I'm setting the parent joints for each leg chain, then plotting the 3D path points for front and hind legs with slight bends at the elbow and knee, and placing the feet along the z-axis. I'm also adding torus-ring wrinkle details near the knees and ankles using a 9-sided polygon profile scaled to the leg radius.

I'm defining a taper function for leg radius that shrinks progressively from thigh to ankle, and considering whether to add a slight bulge near the ankle for a sock-like silhouette before matching it against the foot cylinder's radius.

Checking the hind leg nail counts, then adding shoulder and haunch ellipsoids attached to each leg's root joint for muscle definition. I'm verifying the overall height and length bounds are consistent -- feet resting at y=0, ears and cranium capping around 3.3-3.4, trunk tip extending to about 0.25 -- before finalizing the root return.

Now I'm setting up surface scattering for skin detail cards: using sweep surfaces for the body and legs, scattering crease cards with appropriate size, lean, and spin variation, filtered to avoid low areas and buried points, keeping everything grouped under one mesh per texture for efficiency. I'm also naming the model "African Bush Elephant" as part of the metadata.

Now I'm defining helper types and interpolation functions—a keyframe-based lerp helper, a typed body radius function combining radial keyframes, and a vertical shift function for the silhouette, while being careful to only import what's actually used to avoid TypeScript strictness errors around unused imports.

Still writing helper functions...

I should double check parent-child joint alignment between neck and spine tip, and make sure head parts use the cranium as a surface target for eye placement, being careful about automatic name collisions on unnamed meshes.

For the jaw, I'll give the lower jaw bone its own unique name, then set up the tusk sweep using a curved path from gum to tip with a tapering radius down to a sharp point cap, iterating over both left and right sides.

The slight overlap with the jaw ellipsoid corner seems acceptable. Now I'm writing the full file, including a meta description, and setting up the ear joints with their placement on each side of the head.

Writing extrude parameters...

The short edge near the bottom should still be safe, since smoothing cuts only a quarter from each neighboring edge, and even with cuts from both ends that leaves enough room without crossing into another edge. I'll proceed assuming no corner-cut collision occurs here, though I want to double check to be safe.

I'm sketching the ear rim tube, a hinge flap for the ear, and verifying the ear base position sits correctly inside the cranium without overlapping the eye decal. I'm also planning the hair crown card scatter logic filtered by normal and z-position, and double-checking the Fill type import before writing the chain rings helper code.

Writing ring helper code...

Checking the ring signature for placing items along the tail chain, figuring out the angle convention since the tail hangs mostly vertical.

Setting up the hips joint role and double-checking there's no naming conflict with the hind leg's hip joints before writing the final code.

Adding mud scatter details for the legs with filtered height ranges and spin variation, then verifying type signatures on the scatter and paint functions line up before finalizing the file.

For eyelashes, I'm computing each lash's position and angle using arc math along the eye curve — but I notice the top lash y-coordinates come out negative, pushing them outside the viewBox and getting clipped.

So I'm fixing it by shifting the eye center down to cy=24 with ry=14, recalculating so the topmost lash point lands around y=3.5, well within the 40-unit viewBox. Then I'm laying out the skin-toned eyelid ellipse, the darker eyeball ellipse beneath it, and the iris circle on top.

Now I'm checking the amber iris and pupil placement at cy=24, confirming the decal's aspect ratio of 64:40 matches the intended 0.15x0.094 size on the elephant head, and verifying the decal options object has the required size field. I'm also working out the nostril geometry—placing a small dark circle near the trunk tip using the tangent and binormal vectors from the trunk's chain point to offset it correctly.

Now I'm positioning the trunk tip pad as a cylinder cap slightly larger than the tube radius, extending just beyond the sweep's end along the tangent direction, and setting the cap options for the sweep geometry.

For the finger-like spike, I'm figuring out the base point just forward and slightly below the trunk tip, choosing a muted skin tone close to the pad color, then moving on to double-check the eye placements before finalizing the build.

I need to keep tuple typing consistent for the point arrays feeding the catmull-rom curve, add the nail loop, and verify the hair/crown cards inherit the head bone through the scatter hits. Writing the full file now.
